title: Between any two values
question: What makes a variable continuous?
hook: If you can always fit another possible value between two others, the usual counting tools stop working.
idea: A continuous variable has possible values between any two of its values, which is why calculus and density functions suit it.

beats.prompt: Pick any two values that a continuous variable can take, however close together. What must be true?

choices.label: There are possible values between them
There is a gap with no possible values between them
choices.feedback: That describes a discrete variable, which has a gap around each permitted value.

choices.label: Only one of the two can actually occur
choices.feedback: Nothing in the idea of continuity limits which values can occur.

beats.explain: A continuous variable has possible values between any two values.

beats.prompt: match each situation to the tool that goes with it
beats.explain: Each kind of variable, and each treatment of time, has its own matching description.

items: Any value in a range of the real numbers
beats.explain: Continuous variables fill a range with no gaps; discrete ones have separated permitted values such as integers.

beats.prompt: one step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: A dial can be set to any value between 0 and 1.
Between any two settings there are other possible settings.
So its distribution is expressed with a probability mass function.
beats.explain: Probability density functions express the distributions of continuous variables; mass functions are for discrete ones.
